questions.q: In "Respect and listening Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Avoid pressure and hidden fees.
Who buys now and who else could.
Help the owner name their ten best customers, what each buys and how often, then count how many arrived through recommendation to see which channels work.
Meet the owner in a place they choose.

questions.q: In "Health check Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Set three goals for the 90 days, each with a number and a date, for example 10 new customers by day 60, and display them where the owner will see them daily.
Celebrate small wins in writing.
Measures: sales, orders, customers, savings.
Note strengths before problems.

questions.q: In "Barriers and routes Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Compare with the health check.
Show the owner the true cost of one sale and the smallest price rise that would increase profit, using an actual product from their own sales.
Explain every term in plain language.
Strengths first: skills, products, customers, community.

questions.q: In "Customers and markets Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Celebrate what worked; adjust what did not.
Use the owner's words in every document.
Avoid assumptions and labels.
Test one new market cheaply, such as a market stall or an online listing for two weeks, and record the number of enquiries and sales it produces.

questions.q: In "Money and finance Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Three goals; each with three actions.
Owner, helper, date for each.
Grants, small loans, savings groups, supplier credit.
Meet the owner in a place they choose.

questions.q: In "Skills and tools Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Celebrate small wins in writing.
Explain every term in plain language.
Set three goals for the 90 days, each with a number and a date, for example 10 new customers by day 60, and display them where the owner will see them daily.
Reviews and referrals.

questions.q: In "The 90-day plan Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Score six areas from 1 to 5, such as sales, cash, records, customers, people and tools, to give the owner a simple picture they can understand at a glance.
Offers and prices that fit.
Skills, tools, records, legal basics.
Ask what support is still needed at the end.

questions.q: In "Progress and handover Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: At day 90, compare the starting health-check scores with the new ones and show the owner the changes in a simple table so progress is clearly visible.
Review day 30 and 60.
Strengths first: skills, products, customers, community.
Show the owner the true cost of one sale and the smallest price rise that would increase profit, using an actual product from their own sales.
